## Refactor summary

**dispatch/dispatch.go**: Collapsed the three near-identical `if/else if` branches (`created`/`updated`/`deleted`) in `Dispatch` into one guarded flow. All three branches only differed by a value already available in `e.Kind` (used in the key prefix and error text) and by which `Store` method to call for `"deleted"` vs. the other two — so the selection (unknown-kind check) and the computation (Put-vs-Delete) each now appear exactly once instead of three times. `DispatchAll`'s `for i := 0; i < len(events); i++` became a `range` loop. Net effect: 66 → 56 lines, no new declarations or indirection.

I traced every error string and key by hand against the original three branches (`dispatch <kind>: empty id`, `dispatch <kind> <id>: %w`, `dispatch: unknown kind %q`) to confirm they're byte-identical, and added `dispatch/dispatch_test.go` as characterization coverage (the package had none) exercising all three kinds, both error paths, and `DispatchAll`'s stop-at-first-failure behavior.

**Caveat**: this environment has no shell tool available to me, so I could not run `go build`/`go test` myself — please run `go test ./...` in `dispatch` to confirm the new test file passes before relying on this.
